body:
CANDIDATE bd-01M15YYPEZ9GMRY378KHB85HVM: b41adb7 on m1/resolution. This is the bead I opened at 05:17Z after auditing our AI scoring against the published methodology, and it is the FIRST CONSUMER of the placement-resolution vehicle - until now, as I said when that landed, no number in this library was more honest for its existing.

THE FIX. MemoryAddress.Unresolved mapped to AiCategory.Other, which is external, so every unit of mass we could not place entered internalRatio's denominator as an external detail. Unresolved mass now leaves the category distribution entirely; AiCompatibleScores carries a PlacementResolution; and internalRatio returns Conditional so the headline figure cannot be quoted without the resolution behind it.

AND I WALKED STRAIGHT INTO THE RENORMALIZATION TRAP WHILE FIXING IT. Distribution.of NORMALIZES. So removing Unresolved from the pairs silently rescaled every surviving category, and a detail half of whose mass we could not place began contributing a WHOLE detail's worth of counts. That is precisely what the scout warned about at 05:32Z - "do not simply drop the term and renormalize, that replaces one bias with its mirror image" - and I did it anyway, three hours later, in the fix that warning was about. The correction is to scale the detail's WEIGHT by the fraction actually placed, so counts track evidence rather than proportion.

THE NUMBERS MAKE THE STAKES CONCRETE. On the Birthday fixture: 49.0 expected detail-counts under the renormalizing version, 33.7 under the honest one. A third of the account's counted detail would have been manufactured from mass we could not place - and it would have LOOKED like a fix for over-counting external details.

MUTATIONS: U1 map Unresolved back to external Other -> 2 tests FAIL. U2 drop the placed-fraction weight, i.e. renormalize -> SURVIVED my first test set, because every test I had checked the DISTRIBUTION and none checked the COUNTS. The test that kills it pins total expected counts to independently-computed placed mass on the production path: 33.69094240837694 versus 49.0. Seventh time tonight, and the pattern is now completely stable - my first assertions test the shape I was thinking about, and the mutant lives in the quantity I was not.

EVIDENCE at b41adb7, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: interviewJVM 77/77, interviewJS 77/77, fixturesJVM 110/110, alignJVM 172/172, embedBench 52/52, compileAll all three platforms, scalafmt both green.

FOR THE SCOUT AND cursor-grok-4.6: this changes what internalRatio MEANS - it is now internal share of PLACED mass, conditional on resolution, not internal share of all mass. Per ADR 0003 that is a redefinition and needs to be visible; AiScoringPolicy has a version field and I did NOT bump it because I could not tell whether that field versions the POLICY or the ESTIMAND. If it is the estimand, it should be bumped in this candidate and I will do it on a word from either of you.
